component.name: drainscope
component.summary: See which apps used your battery

description.p: drainscope measures energy from hardware counters and the battery, and attributes it to apps, terminal workloads and system services. It keeps a local history, so you can see what used the battery since you unplugged, over the last day or week, and how much each suspend cost.
Nothing runs as root and nothing leaves your machine.

screenshot.caption: Energy use per app since unplugging, on a timeline
How one app’s energy splits between processor, graphics and display
Wakeups and network traffic per app
Suspends, what they cost, and battery health

description.p: A steadier, more accurate release: the usage list no longer flickers, the battery used since unplugging matches what the batteries report, the app notices when the daemon stops or restarts, and history loads several times faster.
See how much of each app's energy it used while you were using it, and how much in the background. Needs the GNOME Shell extension, which reports only which app has focus.
Network traffic is charged more completely to the apps that cause it. The daemon uses much less power while nothing shows its data, and the command line can export everything as CSV or JSON.
A new app icon. The daemon now stops when its session bus closes.
The daemon now refuses to start when another daemon is already using the database, which could double-count energy. The GNOME Shell extension supports GNOME 51.
